title: Koʻolina Lagoons
paragraphs: Ko'olina Lagoons Photo Courtesy: Aloha Secrets
Location:
Kapolei, O'ahu​
Client:
Aulani
Markets:
Resorts
Photo Courtesy: Dwell Hawaii

For decades, the Aulani Lagoons have been an iconic destination on the western coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Known for their pristine, man-made beauty, the lagoons have been a central feature of the Aulani, A Disney Resort & Spa. This family-friendly resort combines the magic of Disney with the rich cultural heritage of Hawaii, creating a unique and beloved vacation spot.

The Aulani Lagoons, part of the Ko Olina Resort, are a series of four protected lagoons offering calm waters perfect for swimming, snorkeling, and other recreational activities. These lagoons are surrounded by lush landscaping and sandy beaches, providing a serene and picturesque environment for resort guests and visitors.

The land on which the Aulani Lagoons are situated has a rich history, originally used by Hawaiian royalty for relaxation and fishing. Over time, the area has been developed into a luxurious resort destination, while maintaining its natural beauty and cultural significance. The development of the lagoons involved creating safe and sustainable recreational spaces that complement the natural landscape.

The Aulani Resort, operated by Disney, offers a distinctive blend of Hawaiian culture and Disney magic. The resort features upscale accommodations, multiple dining options, a world-class spa, and numerous activities for families and children. The design of the resort incorporates traditional Hawaiian art and storytelling, ensuring that guests experience the local culture throughout their stay.

The development and maintenance of the Aulani Lagoons faced several challenges, including environmental concerns, the preservation of natural habitats, and the integration of sustainable practices. The project team worked closely with environmental experts, local authorities, and cultural advisors to address these challenges. Their collaborative efforts ensured that the lagoons were developed in a manner that respects the natural and cultural heritage of the area.

The installation of the lagoons required careful planning and execution. The project team employed advanced construction techniques to create the man-made lagoons, ensuring they were environmentally sustainable and safe for public use. Regular meetings and open communication between the contractors, designers, and Disney representatives were crucial in overcoming the technical and logistical challenges.

Today, the Aulani Lagoons are a shining example of how modern development can harmonize with natural beauty and cultural heritage. They provide a tranquil and enjoyable experience for visitors, contributing to the resort's reputation as a premier destination in Hawaii. The success of the lagoons and the Aulani Resort highlights the importance of thoughtful planning, collaboration, and respect for the environment in creating sustainable and cherished recreational spaces.

title: Aulani Resort — newer CMS story
paragraphs: Aulani, a Disney Resort & Spa, is a 15-story beachfront property rising about 180 feet at 92-1185 Ali'inui Drive in Ko Olina, Kapolei on Oahu's leeward coast, opened in 2011 as Disney's standalone Hawaiian escape blending Polynesian culture with family magic across 21 acres of lagoons and gardens. It offers 351 hotel rooms plus 481 Disney Vacation Club villas and studios in 1- to 3-bedroom layouts with kitchens, lanais, and ocean or garden views, emphasizing Hawaiian storytelling through art, murals, and 'ohana-focused spaces rather than theme park rides.​

The resort shines with Waikolohe Valley's water playground featuring a lazy river, tube slides (Tubestone Curl and volcano slide), splash zones (Menehune Bridge, Keiki Cove), multiple pools, a private beach cove for gentle waves and snorkeling, plus daily activities like character meets (Mickey, Moana, Stitch), hula lessons, lei-making, and 'Aunty's Beach House kids club. Dining spans 10 outlets from Makahiki buffet to casual 'Ulu spots, with spa treatments, fitness, and Rainbow Reef snorkel lagoon adding relaxation amid Ko Olina's man-made lagoons near golf and Four Seasons.​

From a technical standpoint, the low-rise towers use reinforced concrete for seismic stability in Hawaii's zone, with open-air designs maximizing trade winds for natural cooling and high-performance glazing to frame ocean views while cutting solar heat. Podium-level pools and landscaping integrate stormwater basins and native plants for LEED efficiency, supporting high guest traffic via efficient shuttles from HNL airport (30 minutes away) on a site blending luxury with cultural authenticity

title: Hilton Grand Islander
paragraphs: The Grand Islander, a Hilton Grand Vacations Club, is a 38-story luxury all-suite tower rising about 450 feet at 2023 Kalia Road in Waikiki, Honolulu, integrated into the Hilton Hawaiian Village Waikiki Beach Resort's 22-acre beachfront campus. Opened in phases around 2021-2022, it offers 411 spacious 1-, 2-, and 3-bedroom suites with full kitchens, washer/dryers, living/dining areas, spa-like bathrooms with rain showers and soaking tubs, and private balconies capturing ocean, mountain, or city views, perfect for families seeking home-like comforts amid Waikiki's energy.​

Guests access the full Hilton Hawaiian Village amenities including multiple pools, spas, fitness centers, dining (over 20 outlets), water sports, shopping, and Kahanamoku Lagoon beach just steps away, plus on-site perks like a 3rd-floor pool, cabanas, cultural activities, and a daily resort charge covering WiFi and classes. Its prime spot near Ala Moana Center, Convention Center, and Duke Kahanamoku Statue makes it ideal for conventions, shopping, or beach lounging in Oahu's tourist heart.​

From a technical standpoint, the high-rise uses a reinforced concrete core and steel framing for seismic resilience in Honolulu's zone, with high-performance glazing and curtain walls optimizing natural light and views while managing heat gain via efficient HVAC and LEED features. Multi-elevator banks and podium-level parking support high occupancy, with interiors blending modern chic (water-featured lobby, eco-friendly finishes) and Hawaiian motifs for a resort feel on a compact urban beach site.​
